Hey! We're NORLA 🚀 A team passionate about technology, science, and innovation. We're joining NASA Space Apps 2026 to explore new ideas, learn together, and build something meaningful.

We're interested in AI, software development, data analysis, design, and space science. We're looking for creative, motivated people who enjoy teamwork and aren't afraid of new challenges.

No need to be an expert. Just bring your curiosity and ideas. Let's create something amazing! 🌌
summary:
We've been working on Planetary Intelligence, a scientific project developed by Team NORLA for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
Our goal is to build a scientific workbench that helps users investigate changes on Earth and explore lunar conditions through actual data, statistical analysis, and numerical methods.
The platform brings together three main engines:
Earth Intelligence: NASA POWER data, trend analysis, seasonal analysis, regional comparisons, and data quality diagnostics.
SAR Change Intelligence: Raster inspection and radar-based surface change analysis using GeoTIFF and HDF5 files.
Lunar Intelligence: Meeus-based calculations for lunar illumination, Earth visibility, and optional terrain horizon analysis.
We built the project using React, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, NumPy, and Rasterio, without relying on AI or machine learning for scientific results.
Some limitations remain. SAR demo scenes are synthetic, and real-data processing depends on the input products and backend configuration. Not all documented data sources are connected yet.
We're sharing what we've built so far, including its capabilities and limitations, and there's still more to come.
Explore the project:
https://planetary-intelligence.vercel.app/
Team NORLA | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
details:
Planetary Intelligence – Project Details

Planetary Intelligence is a scientific analysis platform developed by Team NORLA to help users investigate environmental changes on Earth and explore scientific conditions relevant to lunar missions.

The platform goes beyond simply displaying scientific data. Its Earth Intelligence engine allows users to examine environmental variables, analyze historical observations, identify trends, and evaluate their statistical significance. It uses NASA POWER data and applies statistical methods to help distinguish meaningful changes from ordinary variation.

The platform also includes additional analytical capabilities for Earth surface-change investigations and lunar mission analysis. Its lunar engine uses astronomical calculations to examine solar geometry, illumination conditions, and potential communication opportunities at lunar locations.

One of the project's main benefits is making scientific analysis more accessible, transparent, and reproducible. Users can examine the underlying data, understand the methods used, and recognize the assumptions and limitations behind analytical results.

Our approach is based on deterministic scientific calculations rather than AI-generated scientific conclusions. Statistical methods and scientific validation are central to the platform's design.

The project was developed as a modular software platform using web technologies and scientific computing tools. Its design emphasizes accuracy, traceability, usability, and the responsible interpretation of scientific data.

Our goal is to provide researchers, students, and scientifically interested users with a practical environment for exploring planetary and environmental data and turning observations into evidence-based investigations.
